A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, A Unified Approach to Routing and Cascading for LLMs. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 report original evaluations on RouterBench and practical benchmarks. Appendix F also reports ablation and runtime experiments.

after.justification: The original benchmark evaluations and appendix experiments are retained. Figure 4 additionally displays cost–quality curves.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 provide pseudocode for the existing routing, cascading, and cascade-routing procedures. The optimization objectives, randomized selection, stopping decisions, model ordering, and pruning mechanism are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain RouterBench, SWE-Bench, Minerva Math/LiveCodeBench, the classification and open-form benchmarks, and synthetic runtime scenarios. The new worked examples are explanatory, and Figure 4 uses existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain linear interpolation, routing, the threshold-based cascade, and the authors' optimal cascade. Figure 4 uses the same comparator set; newly cited cascading papers are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The model pools, data splits, noise settings, shot counts, and AUC evaluation over cost budgets remain unchanged, including Appendix D. Figure 4 displays the established cost–quality evaluation without introducing a distinct protocol.

E4.justification: The noise-sensitivity analysis in Figure 2, design ablations in Table 7, runtime scaling in Figure 3, and cascading discrepancy analysis in Appendix H are retained. Figure 4 adds benchmark curves without a new ablation or robustness question.

E5.justification: Both versions use sample bootstrapping to estimate uncertainty in AUC differences and report 2σ confidence intervals in Tables 4–6. No changes to statistical procedures, run counts, or seed reporting were identified.

E6.justification: Figure 4 newly reports cost-specific quality curves for five-model RouterBench with medium noise, five-model SWE-Bench, and LLAMA classification. Existing numerical tables and earlier plotted results are unchanged; the addition provides finer-grained results without establishing improved performance over v2.

T1.justification: The definitions, optimality theorems, corollaries, lemmas, assumptions, and proofs are retained. The cascading optimization equation removed from the main text has an equivalent formulation retained in Appendix B; equation renumbering and worked examples do not change the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about optimality, unifying routing and cascading, empirical superiority, and the importance of quality estimation. The shortened conclusion does not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning estimator quality and the failure explanations in Appendix H remain unchanged. The added latency-versus-generation-cost paragraph reiterates cost choices already documented in Appendix D.2.

D1.justification: V3 adds step-by-step pseudocode but removes v2 Section 3's equal-λ binary-search initialization and subsequent Hyperopt tuning instructions and link. Appendix B retains only a generic search description. This is a documentation change, without evidence that the implemented tuning procedure changed.

R1.justification: V3 adds Damani et al. (2024) and Nie et al. (2024), and Sections 3 and 6 more broadly characterize existing cascading approaches as application-specific instantiations of the thresholding scheme. The principal research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Sections 2–4 gain worked examples and algorithm explanations, routing hyperparameter discussion moves to Appendix A, and introductory and concluding passages are shortened. The overall section organization and most existing prose remain stable.

P2.justification: V3 adds three boxed algorithm listings and the three-panel Figure 4. Existing figures and tables retain their designs and content, with some relocated as the text reflows.

improvement.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the worked examples make the procedures easier to follow, while Figure 4 exposes cost-specific tradeoffs previously summarized through AUC. These limited clarity and reporting gains outweigh the loss of the explicit initialization and Hyperopt instructions, although that omission weakens reproducibility. The theoretical and principal empirical evidence remain unchanged.
